summary: Members can now protect their accounts with two-factor authentication from an authenticator app, and sign in with a passkey instead of a password. Passkeys use your fingerprint, face, screen lock or a security key, and cannot be used on a fake copy of the site.
detailed_changes: You can turn on two-factor authentication from Account security by scanning a QR code with an authenticator app. You get 8 single-use recovery codes to keep somewhere safe (#269, #296, #297).
With two-factor on, signing in with a password or an emailed link asks for a 6-digit code. Each code works once, and after 5 wrong codes you have to start signing in again (#298).
If you lose your phone, a recovery code gets you in. You can get a new set of recovery codes or turn two-factor off after confirming it's you, and we email you when either happens (#299).

You can add passkeys from Account security, give each one a name, rename them and remove them. We email you when a passkey is added or removed, and your passkeys are included in your data export (#270, #300, #301).

The sign-in page has a "Sign in with a passkey" button, and supported browsers offer your passkey straight from the email field. A passkey that checks your fingerprint, face or PIN counts as two-factor, so you are not asked for a code as well (#302).
If you use two-factor, you can answer the code step with a passkey instead (#302).
Staff continue to sign in through Cloudron single sign-on, where two-factor is enforced by Cloudron. The sign-in methods Cloudron reports are now recorded in the audit log (#303).
affected_areas: User groups affected: members who sign in with a password or emailed link; staff sign-in is unchanged
Public impact: optional two-factor authentication, recovery codes, passkey management and passkey sign-in, new security emails
Internal impact: new passkeys table and two-factor columns on users, new audit events, Cloudron staff two-factor documented, governance records updated
